obligations.statement: The acceptance field selects one canonical, reproducible rendered contract.
obligations.source: LIFE-D1: “The field selects; the renderer resolves,” followed by the rendering and resolution rules.

parts.statement: Full text, citations, and mixed input resolve in field order from the named spec, including continuation text and later cited-spec edits.
Explicit IDs survive, while generated IDs are stable, unique, and valid in the consumer grammar.
Each generated ID is deterministically derived from the item ID and the text line's nonblank position.
An empty cited entry contributes no criterion.
Unresolved or duplicate IDs, collisions, and missing, unreadable, or unparseable specs are refused with the offending ID or path and cause.
The rendering separates description context from criteria so consumers recover only the criteria section.
Rendering depends only on description, acceptance, and named spec and is independent of working directory and unrelated metadata.
Workcli and spec-lint remain compatible counterparts over the common round-trip fixture.
Spec delivery stores assigned criterion IDs as citations rather than copied text.

obligations.statement: Every item is attacked against the correct canonical document and uses the required stored attack artifacts.
obligations.source: LIFE-D2 defines spec-born and tracker-born documents, paths, workflow, reuse, and generated-directory behavior.

parts.statement: Citation-only items attack the whole spec; any full-text acceptance line makes the item attack its rendering.
The tracker-born workflow renders and attacks at the prescribed paths, commits only after checker success, attests afterward, and leaves no committed artifacts or attestation on failure.
Unchanged files with valid current evidence are reused without another model round.
The generated attack directory exists in a fresh checkout and is exempt from authored-prose doc-lint.
Editing a generated rendering does not amend the contract and cannot establish a valid tracker-born attestation unless it equals a fresh rendering.
An empty selection remains unusable at gated transitions even when its spec has been attacked.

obligations.statement: Attestation binds an item to the current attacked bytes and rejects invalid evidence safely.
obligations.source: LIFE-D3 defines the marker, binding and closure refusals, idempotence, fresh-render checks, and consuming-boundary behavior.

parts.statement: A valid closed record creates one usable content-revision attestation, including under repeated or concurrent requests.
A rename with unchanged bytes preserves attestation after references and the canonical record binding are updated.
Every listed binding or closure violation is refused without writing a marker.
Consumers compute current state, ignore malformed markers, and name unreadable marker sources.
The facade enforces binding and closure without independently classifying criterion meaning.

obligations.statement: Amendments invalidate stale evidence and require a fresh attack before reuse.
obligations.source: LIFE-D4 defines invalidation, the amendment trail, full re-attack, and before-use behavior.

parts.statement: A tracker-born change that changes rendered bytes makes the prior attestation unusable.
Any attacked-spec byte change invalidates every citing item, while changing only a spec-born item's description does not.
An acceptance-field amendment uses work acceptance set --why and records its reason trail.
Changed attacked documents are rerendered where needed, fully attacked, committed, and attested before reuse, including editorial and unrelated-spec changes.
Dispatch and review-halt instructions state the quality standard and before-use re-attack rule.

obligations.statement: Claim, delivery, review, and posting apply the defined criteria and attestation gates without interpreting criterion prose.
obligations.source: LIFE-D5 supplies the transition table and structural-role behavior; LIFE-D6 applies the review and posting boundaries.

parts.statement: Every open-to-in-progress verb applies the noun and triviality claim rules.
PR delivery requires resolvable criteria for every leaf and current attestation for every nontrivial leaf.
Review emission and verdict posting apply their corresponding current-rendering and attestation rows.
An already-in-progress claim remains a no-op.
Installing the facade does not rewrite existing items.
Refusals identify the prescribed remedy or failing ID, path, or attack step.
Gates do not classify criteria by wording.
A design child bypasses claim and delivery criteria and attestation gates.
Structural children of a spec container have no noun.
An implementation placeholder is unclaimable.
An implementation placeholder is retired when the spec manifest expands.
An item with neither a recognized noun nor a recognized structural role is refused by type at claim and delivery.

obligations.statement: Review artifacts contain exactly the current rendered contract that was judged.
obligations.source: LIFE-D6 defines fresh review input, recorded judged bytes, posting comparisons, amendment behavior, and the no-item path.

parts.statement: Review emission accepts only a fresh admissible rendering and records those bytes with the round.
Posting requires equality with both the judged input and a fresh admissible rendering, including after re-attacked amendments.
The poster extracts only the acceptance-criteria section and never falls back to unchecked item content.
A review target with no work item retains the supplied-file path.

obligations.statement: CI validates the complete tracked attack-record inventory deterministically and fails safely when it cannot do so.
obligations.source: LIFE-D7 defines the inventory, invalid states, dependency failures, checkout boundary, and required-lens migration.

parts.statement: One run reports every invalid tracked record and its cause, including missing attacked documents and paths.
A missing checker or failed inventory enumeration prevents success.
Ignored, untracked, and other-checkout records are excluded, and an empty tracked inventory passes when the checker is available.
The check is deterministic and does not modify an unchanged checkout.
Once a changed attacked document is committed, CI remains red until its record closes at that revision.
A newly required lens is not enforced on the default branch until existing committed records have been migrated.

obligations.statement: Adoption uses the existing facade and delivery architecture with explicit version compatibility.
obligations.source: LIFE-D8 assigns component ownership, version checks, Claude-only rounds, cross-tool handoff, and briefing content.

parts.statement: Consumers establish a semantically sufficient installed facade version before invoking new verbs, name failures, and do not mutate item state during the check.
Render, attest, claim, and delivery changes are implemented in the workcli repository.
The attack and review skills remain Claude-only.
Other tools hand attack and review rounds to a Claude Code session through the existing delivery workflow.
Briefs cite the quality standard and the before-use amendment rule.

obligations.statement: Lifecycle testing does not mutate deployed configuration or the user's tracker.
obligations.source: Testing decisions: “No test deploys configuration or rewrites the user's tracker.”

parts.statement: No lifecycle test deploys configuration or rewrites the user's tracker.

obligations.statement: Component child specs close component contracts without weakening the parent design.
obligations.source: Testing decisions: “Component child specs define wire formats and fixtures before scaffolding. They retain these public contracts and may not weaken parent invariants or leave significant product decisions to implementation.”

parts.statement: Each component child spec defines its wire formats and fixtures before scaffolding.
Component child specs retain the parent public contracts, preserve its invariants, and resolve significant product decisions before implementation.

ground.reason: User story 5 promises that a verdict reader can see exactly which criteria were judged. LIFE-A17 checks only whether posting rejects stale or mismatched criteria. It does not require the posted verdict artifact to expose those criteria to the reader.

objections.objection: A poster can validate the judged criteria correctly and then publish a verdict that omits them, satisfying LIFE-A17 while the promised reader outcome is absent.
objections.obligation: A verdict reader can see exactly the criteria judged.

scenario.given: A verdict whose supplied criteria match both the recorded review input and the fresh rendering
scenario.when: The poster validates the criteria and publishes a verdict that does not include them
scenario.expect: The LIFE-A17 posting checks pass, but the reader cannot see which criteria were judged

ground.reason: LIFE-D1 promises compatible workcli and spec-lint grammars across repositories. LIFE-A28 checks only that both parsers return the same entries for one shared fixture. Agreement on that artifact does not establish agreement for every input allowed by the resolution rules.

objections.objection: The parsers can special-case or merely agree on the shared fixture while disagreeing on another valid rendering.
objections.obligation: Workcli and spec-lint interpret the resolution grammar compatibly.

scenario.given: Two parsers that agree on the shared fixture but handle a different valid continuation or citation combination differently
scenario.when: The LIFE-A28 fixture check runs
scenario.expect: The fixture check passes while cross-repository grammar compatibility is absent

ground.reason: LIFE-A24 requires that gates never reject qualifying criteria because of their wording. The testing decisions name the fake backend but provide no input domain, generated cases, structural invariant, or other rule capable of deciding this universal claim.

objections.objection: A gate can contain a wording-dependent rejection that lies outside the unspecified test examples and still be accepted.
objections.obligation: Claim and delivery gates do not classify or reject criterion prose by wording.

scenario.given: An implementation that rejects otherwise valid criteria only when they contain an untested phrase
scenario.when: The unspecified LIFE-A24 acceptance check runs using ordinary sample wording
scenario.expect: The sampled checks pass while a wording-dependent refusal remains

ground.reason: LIFE-A4 combines a renderer output requirement with behavior required from separate downstream consumers. The heading structure and consumer extraction can be implemented and accepted independently.

objections.objection: The renderer half can be delivered while existing consumers still parse criterion-shaped description text.
objections.obligation: Renderer structure and consumer section isolation are separate obligations.

scenario.given: A renderer that emits the description under the required heading, paired with a consumer that scans the entire rendering
scenario.when: The renderer-output part of LIFE-A4 is checked
scenario.expect: The renderer check passes while the consumer still treats criterion-shaped description text as criteria

ground.reason: LIFE-A15 combines exemption behavior at two distinct public transitions: claim and delivery. Either transition can implement or violate the exemption independently.

objections.objection: A design child can bypass the claim gates but still be refused by the delivery gates.
objections.obligation: Design-child claim exemption and design-child delivery exemption are separate obligations.

scenario.given: A design child without criteria or attestation whose claim path recognizes the structural role but whose delivery path does not
scenario.when: The claim exemption is checked
scenario.expect: Claim passes while the independently deliverable delivery exemption is absent

ground.reason: LIFE-A26 combines type refusal at claim with type refusal at delivery. These are separate boundaries with independently implementable dispatch and error paths.

objections.objection: Unknown item types can be rejected at claim while remaining deliverable.
objections.obligation: Unknown-type refusal at claim and at delivery are separate obligations.

scenario.given: An item with neither a recognized noun nor a recognized structural role, with type validation implemented only for claim
scenario.when: The claim type check runs
scenario.expect: Claim is correctly refused while delivery still accepts the same unknown type

ground.reason: LIFE-A32 combines two independently maintained instruction surfaces: dispatch briefs and instructions following a criteria-indicting review halt. Either surface can carry both required references without the other doing so.

objections.objection: Dispatch briefs can contain the required guidance while review-halt instructions omit it.
objections.obligation: Brief guidance and review-halt guidance are separate obligations.

scenario.given: Updated dispatch briefs that cite both the quality standard and reattack rule, with unchanged review-halt instructions
scenario.when: The dispatch-brief content check runs
scenario.expect: The brief check passes while the review-halt instruction obligation remains unmet

ground.reason: LIFE-A36 combines deterministic reporting with filesystem non-mutation. The gate can satisfy either property independently of the other.

objections.objection: A gate can return the same result twice while writing cache or stamp files into the checkout.
objections.obligation: Repeatable results and read-only execution are separate obligations.

scenario.given: A gate that writes the same cache file on every invocation and returns the same result
scenario.when: Two runs over the unchanged checkout are compared
scenario.expect: The result-equality check passes while the no-write outcome is absent

ground.reason: The criteria require generated IDs to be stable, unique, and syntactically valid, but none requires the ID to be derived from the item ID and the line's nonblank position.

objections.objection: A renderer can use a stable hash of the criterion text for generated IDs and pass every criterion while violating the specified positional-ID rule.

scenario.given: A text-only acceptance field whose renderer passes LIFE-A2 and the shared fixture check
scenario.when: The renderer generates a stable, unique ID from the text content instead of its item and position
scenario.expect: The generated ID is derived from the item ID and the text line's nonblank position.

ground.reason: No criterion observes that a cited spec entry with no content contributes no rendered criterion. Parser agreement in LIFE-A28 does not establish the required behavior.

objections.objection: Both parsers can agree on an empty emitted criterion, allowing all criteria to pass while the renderer violates the empty-entry rule.

scenario.given: A named spec containing a cited entry whose criterion body is empty
scenario.when: The item is rendered and the implementation emits an empty criterion bullet
scenario.expect: The empty cited entry contributes no criterion.

ground.reason: The criteria test invalidation after a field change but never require acceptance-field amendments to use the existing work acceptance set --why trail.

objections.objection: Acceptance text can be changed without recording the required amendment reason while every invalidation and re-attack criterion still passes.

scenario.given: A tracker-born item with current evidence and an implementation satisfying every lifecycle criterion
scenario.when: Its acceptance field is amended through another write path and then rerendered, attacked, and attested
scenario.expect: The amendment is made through work acceptance set --why and leaves its reason trail.

ground.reason: No criterion checks the preservation guarantee that installing the facade leaves existing work items unchanged.

objections.objection: Installation can rewrite existing item fields while the renderer, version checks, and all later transition gates satisfy their criteria.

scenario.given: A repository containing existing work items and an implementation that passes LIFE-A1 through LIFE-A37
scenario.when: The user installs the facade
scenario.expect: Existing work items remain byte-for-byte unchanged by facade installation.

ground.reason: The role-specific criteria cover gate behavior but do not require structural children of a spec container to remain nounless.

objections.objection: Structural children can acquire nouns and be special-cased by role, satisfying LIFE-A15 and LIFE-A25 while violating the stated structural model.

scenario.given: A spec container with a design child and an implementation placeholder
scenario.when: The implementation assigns recognized nouns to both children but preserves the criterion-specified claim and delivery outcomes
scenario.expect: The structural children have no noun.

ground.reason: LIFE-A25 requires an implementation placeholder to be refused at claim, but no criterion requires its retirement when the spec manifest expands.

objections.objection: The placeholder can remain indefinitely after concrete implementation work is created.

scenario.given: A spec whose manifest has expanded into concrete implementation children
scenario.when: All acceptance checks run while the original placeholder remains open and unclaimable
scenario.expect: The implementation placeholder is retired.

ground.reason: The CI criteria require use of the current lens registry, but none enforces the migration ordering that updates existing records before a newly required lens reaches the default branch.

objections.objection: A new required lens can be enabled first, making the default branch's existing records invalid, while the CI gate correctly reports those failures and passes its own criteria.

scenario.given: A default branch with records valid under the old required-lens registry
scenario.when: A registry change requiring another lens lands without migrating those records
scenario.expect: Existing committed records are updated before the new lens requirement is enforced on the default branch.

ground.reason: No criterion observes the architectural allocation that render, attest, claim, and delivery behavior belongs to the workcli repository.

objections.objection: The complete behavior can be implemented in another component and still satisfy every behavioral criterion.

scenario.given: An implementation exposing all required commands and outcomes
scenario.when: The implementation places the behavior in an agents-config skill or another repository instead of workcli
scenario.expect: The facade behaviors are implemented in the workcli repository.

ground.reason: No criterion preserves the stated Claude-only placement of the attack and review skills.

objections.objection: The skills can be deployed directly to every supported tool while all lifecycle behavior remains green.

scenario.given: A lifecycle implementation passing all criteria
scenario.when: The installer also deploys those skills to Codex, Gemini, or OpenCode
scenario.expect: The attack and review skills remain Claude-only.

ground.reason: No criterion checks that non-Claude tools hand attack and review rounds to a Claude Code session through the existing delivery workflow.

objections.objection: A non-Claude tool can fail the round or run an unrelated local substitute without violating any stated criterion.

scenario.given: A non-Claude tool reaches an attack or review round and all facade/version criteria pass
scenario.when: The tool attempts the round without the required handoff
scenario.expect: The round is handed to a Claude Code session through the existing delivery workflow.

ground.reason: The document promises that tests do not deploy configuration or rewrite the user's tracker, but no criterion observes either forbidden side effect.

objections.objection: A test suite can pass every acceptance check while mutating deployed configuration or the user's real tracker.

scenario.given: A passing test suite for LIFE-A1 through LIFE-A37
scenario.when: A test invokes a real deployment path or writes through the user's tracker backend
scenario.expect: The test run leaves deployed configuration and the user's tracker unchanged.

ground.reason: No criterion checks that component child specs define their wire formats and fixtures before scaffolding.

objections.objection: Implementation can begin with wire formats and fixtures invented in production code while every parent acceptance criterion eventually passes.

scenario.given: A component slice whose finished behavior satisfies all assigned parent criteria
scenario.when: Its scaffolding and implementation are created before those contracts appear in the child spec
scenario.expect: The component child spec defines the wire format and fixtures before scaffolding begins.

ground.reason: No criterion evaluates whether component child specs preserve the parent contracts and close significant product decisions before implementation.

objections.objection: A child spec can weaken a parent invariant or delegate a significant decision to implementation even if the eventual implementation happens to satisfy the parent criteria.

scenario.given: A child spec and implementation whose observed behavior passes all parent acceptance checks
scenario.when: The child spec weakens an invariant or leaves a significant decision to the implementer
scenario.expect: The child spec retains every parent invariant and resolves significant product decisions.

ground.reason: LIFE-A17 requires posting to compare the verdict's criteria against 'the round's judged input' recorded at emission, but nothing in the criteria set covers rounds emitted before emission-bytes recording existed. LIFE-D5 states installing the facade does not rewrite existing items while later review and posting still apply their gates, so a pre-migration round has no recorded input to compare against. The criteria leave open whether posting treats a missing recorded input as a mismatch (refuse, forcing a fresh review round for every in-flight review) or as unverifiable and accepted (letting an unrecorded verdict post against any current rendering). Each reading produces a different outcome for the same state.

objections.objection: The criteria admit both refusal and acceptance when a verdict from a round that predates emission-input recording is posted, so the migration behaviour for in-flight reviews is undecidable from the set.

scenario.given: A review round emitted before the facade upgrade, so the round carries no recorded judged-criteria bytes; the named item has nonempty resolvable criteria and a current attestation, and its rendering has not changed.
scenario.when: The verdict poster is invoked to post that round's verdict naming the item.
scenario.expect: Under the 'missing recorded input is a mismatch' reading the post is refused and the review must be re-run; under the 'no recorded input, nothing to contradict' reading the post is accepted. LIFE-A17 and LIFE-D5 together do not select one.

ground.reason: LIFE-A17 says posting 'refuses exactly when the criteria differ from the round's judged input or from a fresh rendering' and that 'this holds after an amendment has been re-attacked'; LIFE-D6 adds that 'a re-attacked amendment still needs a new review of the amended criteria.' If the acceptance field is amended and then reverted to exactly the previously judged bytes, the re-attacked record closes at the current digest and the old verdict's judged input equals a fresh rendering, so the byte-matching reading of LIFE-A17 accepts the old verdict. The amendment-event reading of 'this holds after an amendment has been re-attacked' refuses it because an amendment occurred and was re-attacked. The set does not say whether 'amendment' is a byte difference at posting time or a historical event, and each reading yields the opposite verdict for the same state.

objections.objection: The criteria admit both acceptance and refusal of an old verdict after criteria were amended, re-attacked, and then reverted to the originally judged bytes.

scenario.given: A tracker-born item whose criteria were reviewed (round R), then amended and fully re-attacked, then edited back to byte-identical criteria and re-attacked again; the current fresh rendering equals round R's recorded judged input and a current attestation exists.
scenario.when: The verdict poster is invoked to post round R's verdict naming the item.
scenario.expect: Byte-matching reading: the post is accepted since the judged input equals the fresh rendering. Amendment-event reading: the post is refused because an amendment was re-attacked and LIFE-D6 demands a new review of the amended criteria. The set selects neither.

ground.reason: LIFE-D1 makes the canonical contract the field's selection after resolution, and LIFE-D4's amendment doctrine is 'before use, and again after amendment', but attestation binds only to the attacked document's bytes (LIFE-D3), and for a spec-born item that document is the whole spec (LIFE-D2). LIFE-A9 invalidates on spec-byte changes and LIFE-A8 on tracker-born rendering changes; no criterion invalidates when a spec-born item's citation selection changes while the spec's bytes do not. Claim and delivery (LIFE-A11–A14) check attestation currency, so they pass on evidence for a contract that no longer exists.

objections.objection: The criteria let a spec-born item's contract be amended — different cited criteria claimed, reviewed, and delivered — with zero re-attack, because every invalidation rule keys on attacked-document bytes and the selection lives only in the field. This defeats user story 4 (amendments invalidate evidence for the old contract) at the two boundaries that have no rendering-freshness check.

scenario.given: A spec-born item citing criteria LIFE-A1 and LIFE-A2 of an attacked spec, holding a current attestation bound to the spec's digest.
scenario.when: An amendment via `work acceptance set --why` rewrites the field to cite LIFE-A1 and LIFE-A3, leaving the spec's bytes untouched.
scenario.expect: The old attestation becomes unusable and claim/delivery refuse until the amended selection is judged; instead the marker still matches the spec digest, the rendering is never consulted at those gates, and the item claims and delivers on criteria no attack or review round ever saw.

ground.reason: LIFE-A18 and LIFE-D7 define the CI inventory as every tracked attack record in the checkout, and LIFE-A22 creates tracker-born rendering and record files, but no criterion states what happens to those committed files when their owning item disappears or stops being tracker-born. The stale-rendering remedy in LIFE-D2 (update the item and render again) presupposes the item exists and remains tracker-born.

objections.objection: The criteria let orphaned tracker-born attack artifacts accumulate as permanent CI inventory: the gate must keep validating records for documents nothing uses, and any later touch of a dead rendering fails the gate on an artifact with no owner and no specified removal path.

scenario.given: An item attacked as tracker-born, with `.work/attacks/<item-id>.md` and its record committed and attested.
scenario.when: The item's acceptance field is rewritten to pure spec citations (reclassifying it spec-born under LIFE-D2) or the item is deleted outright, leaving the committed files behind.
scenario.expect: A defined disposition for the orphaned rendering and record — removal, exemption, or continued validity — which no criterion states; the CI gate inventories them forever and the document neither covers nor rules out the case.

ground.reason: LIFE-A22 fixes the order render, attack, commit, then attest, and LIFE-A37 specifies the failure state only for attack or checker failure. The failure path of the final attestation step — after the files are committed — is unnamed: no criterion states the resulting state or that a retry completes the attestation. LIFE-A34 covers reuse of unchanged files and current evidence, but whether a run whose only missing piece is the marker reaches attestation again is left to implication.

objections.objection: The criteria let the tracker-born workflow terminate in an unspecified half-state — committed rendering and record, no attestation, item unclaimable — with no pinned retry behavior, so two implementations can disagree on whether the next invocation re-attacks, re-attests, or refuses.

scenario.given: A tracker-born attack run whose checker has reported the record complete and whose rendering and record have just been committed.
scenario.when: `work acceptance attacked` refuses (for example an unreadable marker source or a binding violation detected only at attest time).
scenario.expect: A defined end state and recovery: the workflow reports the item as committed-but-unattested and the next invocation attests from the reused record without a new attack round; no criterion states either.

dispositions.rationale: Earlier rounds rejected this ground. Agreement on every possible input is a universal claim with no finite check. LIFE-A28 requires the shared fixture to exercise every resolution rule in LIFE-D1, which is the checkable form of that compatibility.

LIFE-A15 states one rule: a design child is outside the criteria and attestation gates. Claim and delivery are two observations of that one obligation, as the standard's one-obligation rule keeps together the observations one obligation needs.

LIFE-A26 states one rule: an item with no recognized noun or role is refused by type. Claim and delivery are two observations of that one obligation, as the standard's one-obligation rule keeps together the observations one obligation needs.
Earlier rounds rejected this ground. LIFE-A2 holds the observable constraints: stable, unique and grammar-valid IDs. The derivation inputs are the spelling LIFE-D1 leaves to the component spec.
Earlier rounds rejected this ground. The --why trail is existing `work acceptance set` behaviour, and nothing in this spec changes it.
Earlier rounds rejected this ground. No slice includes a migration, so no implementation step could rewrite existing items.
Structural children of a spec container are created by the existing `work promote` verb, which this spec does not change.
Earlier rounds rejected this ground. Placeholder retirement is existing facade behaviour (`work deliver --spec` reconciles a design child's placeholder), and this spec does not change it.
Earlier rounds rejected this ground. This is the procedure for a future lens change, and no slice here builds it.
Earlier rounds rejected this ground. Component placement is judged in PR review. It is not behaviour an acceptance check can observe.
The attack and review skills are already Claude-only, and no slice here changes where they deploy.
Earlier rounds rejected this ground. Claude-only rounds and their handoff are existing behaviour, unchanged here.
Earlier rounds rejected this ground. The testing decisions govern how the implementation is tested, and PR review judges them.
Earlier rounds rejected this ground. The lifecycle's own gates and each child spec's attack round enforce these on the child specs.
Earlier rounds rejected this ground. The lifecycle's own gates and each child spec's attack round enforce these on the child specs.

Every criterion a spec-born item can cite was attacked with the whole spec, so a changed selection uses no unattacked text. LIFE-D2 assigns the judgment of selection to the spec's review of its slice assignments, and the change itself goes through the existing --why trail.

Earlier rounds rejected this ground. An orphaned rendering and record pair is unchanged, so it still closes and the CI gate stays green. Removing an orphan is an ordinary deletion, which leaves the gate nothing to check.
